title: Rewards that fit your identity
header_line: Jose's analysis of a book we are still naming. Not a summary of the book. Not affiliated with or endorsed by the author or publisher.

lines.text: What reward do you give yourself that undoes what you just did?
Jose asked what short-term rewards can carry you toward a long-term goal, as when you start training for something that will take a year. A student said: enjoy the process more than the end result.
Jose said the book gives a massage as a short-term reward after hard training.

groups.heading: A reward that fits who you are

lines.text: A student described the book's idea of a dedicated bank account: every time you resist the urge to do the habit you are quitting, you put five dollars into a fund for something you want. You are re-anchoring the experience to something satisfying instead of a drain.

Jose said that what he learned is: do not reward a hard workout with a treat that goes against your identity. He said that is how we were programmed as children: if you eat your dinner, you get dessert.
What is a reward that supports who you want to be?

exercise.title: Five minutes
steps: Write a habit you want to keep.
Write the reward you give yourself now.
Write whether it supports or undoes your identity.
Write a reward that supports it.
Write what you would put in a dedicated fund.

check.q: What did a student say to enjoy more?
What did the student describe for rewards?
What did Jose say not to do after a hard workout?

recap: Reward the process. Choose rewards that fit who you want to be.
